what: Permanent route-maintenance system: nightly source monitor, route-scoped hold record + verifier, weekly/monthly/quarterly review assembler, and the 11-step source-change response procedure. No orchestration platform; machines observe and assemble, people decide.
whatTheNightlyDoes: Assembles 63 monitor targets: all 40 SOURCE_ACQUISITION_MANIFEST.json entries (28 with pinned sha256, 12 observe-only) plus 23 official-source-registry rows whose expectedFrom source-record resolves to an exact https URL and expected hash.

Filters every URL through scripts/lib/official-host-policy.mjs (the one importable host-policy module the acquisition path uses); non-allowlisted hosts are recorded as skipped and never fetched; redirects are followed hop-by-hop and an off-allowlist or off-exact-host redirect is refused and reported.

Records status, redirect chain, content-type, byte length, observed sha256; compares to the pin; outcomes: unchanged / changed_hash / changed_landing_page / vanished_or_unreachable / observed_unpinned / skipped_by_host_policy.

Writes a dated report artifact every run; ONLY on change/loss writes review-task JSON (intendedCommitPath data/rcap-grade-a/maintenance/review-tasks/<date>-<sourceId>.json) into the artifact and opens one GitHub issue per changed source, label source-change-review, deduped by title against open issues.

Derives routesUsing at runtime by joining data/rcap-ledger/launch-graph.json + data/record-clearing/legal-design-packet-set-manifests.json + manifest obligationKeys — generator-owned registries were NOT hand-edited.
whatTheNightlyDoesNot: commit anything (workflows never commit here; review tasks reach the repo only via a person's reviewed commit)
auto-approve, auto-invalidate, or adopt observed bytes
place a hold or touch any route state, registry, or production resource
fetch from non-allowlisted hosts or follow redirects off the allowlist

routeHolds.record: data/rcap-grade-a/maintenance/route-holds.json — single route-scoped hold carrier; header states why it is legitimate (ConsumerDeliveryRouteState is path-wide, release-readiness deploymentReadiness is config-completeness; neither can hold one route) and that RM-1's availability derivation consumes it read-tolerantly.
routeHolds.verifier: scripts/verify-rcap-route-holds.mjs — schema, exact-scope (refuses wildcards, bare jurisdiction codes, 'ALL', unknown pathwayKeys against the launch graph), release discipline (no released hold without a reacceptance reference; reacceptance repo paths must exist), no duplicate active same-type holds; wired into npm test with --mutations.

review: scripts/rcap-maintenance-review.mjs assembles the packet from existing records (open source-change-review issues via API when token present, else last monitor report, else says so; unfinished routes from launch-graph incl. closest-to-done top 25; active holds; stale-artifact-block, problematic-pdf-register, verifier-dispositions) and publishes artifact + step summary. Scope auto resolves weekly/monthly/quarterly by date from one weekly cron; dispatch can force any scope. No state changes.

validationsRun.rcap-source-monitor.mjs --dry-run (no ne: pass, exit 0 — 63 targets, 63 fetchable under host policy, 0 skipped, 0 config problems; plan JSON written
validationsRun.verify-rcap-route-holds.mjs: OK — 0 rows, schema and discipline checks green on the empty record
validationsRun.verify-rcap-route-holds.mjs --mutations: OK — 14/14 planted defects detected (wildcard, jurisdiction-wide, CA:*, ALL, unknown route, bad holdType, empty reason, missing evidence, released-without-reacceptance, released-before-placed, missing reacceptance path, duplicate active hold, premature reacceptance, wrong schemaVersion)
validationsRun.rcap-maintenance-review.mjs --scope week: pass — packets written, tolerant fallbacks exercised (no token, no monitor report)
validationsRun.workflow YAML: actionlint unavailable; both workflows parsed with js-yaml (jobs + on triggers verified)
validationsRun.live fetch: not run from this session (proxy egress 403 to court hosts); the GitHub runner performs the real fetches, and --dry-run is the committed no-network validation

invariants: Nothing scheduled commits to branches, touches production, or auto-changes route state.
One host-policy module governs acquisition and monitoring alike.

A changed hash creates a review task and an issue; every determination above 'the bytes differ' belongs to a person (docs/rcap/EVERGREEN_ROUTE_MAINTENANCE.md, 11 steps, each mapped to its script/workflow or marked a human decision).
